seoBlocs.titre: Bespoke metalwork in Saumur and Anjou

paragraphes: Auboiacier is a metalwork and ironwork workshop opening in Saumur, in Maine-et-Loire, France. We design and make bespoke pieces in steel, solid wood and stainless steel: window railings, staircases, steel internal windows, tables, backlit ceilings and sculptures, for homes, flats and studios in Saumur, Anjou and the Loire Valley. If you are looking for a metalworker in Saumur, you deal directly with the workshop that designs and welds your piece, with no middleman. English spoken.

The workshop makes window railings in solid steel, with St Andrew's crosses, rosettes and a handrail in wood or steel, in the spirit of old balconies; steel spine staircases, built on a heavy steel tube and fitted with solid wood treads; steel internal windows, measured at your home and welded in the workshop; solid wood tables on welded steel bases; backlit stretch-fabric ceiling lights; and sculptures in reclaimed steel, welded piece by piece.
Every piece is bespoke: drawn to your dimensions, then made in Saumur, to order, with no stock and no production runs. You choose the wood, the colour of the steel and the finish.

blocs.h3: Careful making, down to the finish
paragraphes: The steel is cut, hand-welded and ground for a clean surface, then painted in the colour of your choice. The solid wood, whether oak, walnut, beech or pine, is sanded and oiled in the workshop before it is fixed to the steel. The workshop works wood to the same standard as steel, drawing on experience in cabinetmaking, from choosing the boards to the finish.

Window railings are calculated to meet the French building code and the NF P01-012 standard: protective height, gaps between the bars, resistance to loads. The fixing is chosen for your wall (concrete, brick, stone...) and supplied in stainless steel; the railing arrives ready to fit, with its fixings and an installation guide. The light ceilings follow the same standard: an aluminium box welded in the workshop, a stretched fabric and integrated LED lighting, sized to your room.

The price is shown before any appointment. For a window railing, a table or a light ceiling, you enter your measurements in the online configurator: the price appears at once, worked out for your dimensions, and you download a PDF quote with no account and no commitment. For a railing, the configurator works out the height and the gaps between the bars from your window.

A staircase, a steel internal window or a sculpture is priced by quote, and the workshop comes to measure at your home, by appointment: a home measuring visit costs {prixVisite} within {rayonVisite} km of Saumur, and more beyond that, depending on distance. You can also book it for a window railing if you would rather not measure yourself. Every piece is made to order, and the lead time is confirmed to you in writing when you place the order.

From Saumur, the workshop travels across Anjou and Touraine to measure up: in Saumur and the nearby towns of Montreuil-Bellay, Doué-en-Anjou and Fontevraud-l'Abbaye, then in Angers, Tours or Chinon, and up to 200 km from the workshop, across Maine-et-Loire, Indre-et-Loire, Deux-Sèvres and Vienne. Pieces from the collection are delivered by carrier across mainland France; a table arrives unassembled, ready to screw together. Fitting by the workshop, if you want it, is priced in the quote. For metalwork in Saumur or anywhere in the Loire Valley, write to us with your town and your project.

artisanat.faqDeliveryQ: What are the lead and delivery times?
artisanat.faqDeliveryA: Each piece is made to order. The time is shown on the piece's own page, on the “Lead time” line: from 3 to 12 weeks depending on the model — a chair leaves sooner than a staircase. Then comes delivery across mainland France (assembly is included if you choose fitting by the workshop); we propose a precise slot as soon as your piece is ready.
artisanat.faqCareQ: How do I care for a wood & steel piece?
artisanat.faqCareA: A soft dry cloth day to day. For oiled wood, re-apply hardwax oil once a year; scratches sand out lightly. Painted steel wipes clean with a damp sponge — no abrasives.
artisanat.deliveryTitle: Delivery across mainland France, fitting optional
artisanat.deliveryBody: We deliver anywhere in mainland France by carrier: the price depends on your town, the weight and the size, and appears on the product page as soon as you enter your postcode. The piece travels protected, and we agree a precise time slot with you. The piece arrives with its notes; a table arrives dismantled, ready to screw together (top, base, hardware). If you would rather the workshop delivered and fitted it itself, choose that on the product page: the price depends on the distance from Saumur, and it all happens in a single trip.

apropos.title: About
apropos.h1: Steel and solid wood, made to last.
apropos.intro: Auboiacier is a metalwork workshop opening in Saumur, in the Loire Valley. Every piece is made to measure, to order.
apropos.facon: Each piece is born in the Saumur workshop, to your measurements. The steel is cut and welded there, the solid wood cut to size and oiled, every finish completed by hand down to the last detail. Made to stand the test of time.
apropos.prix: The price is clear, and you know it before you order: online for most pieces, on a quote for the others. A fair price, so that work done properly stays within reach.
apropos.homme: A metalworker and welder, I worked in France and then in Australia, on projects of every size, before founding Auboiacier in Saumur. Railings, staircases, steel internal windows, furniture, backlit ceilings: every piece is designed to your measurements, welded and finished to the same standard, in steel and solid wood, to last. I have also worked in cabinetmaking: I work solid wood to the same standard as steel, from choosing the boards to the finish.
apropos.parcours: You have a single point of contact, from measuring to delivery, and a price stated clearly before any order.

cgv.title: Terms and conditions of sale
cgv.intro: These terms govern sales made on auboiacier.fr. They are accepted by the customer before any payment.

sections.title: 1. The seller
sections.body: Auboiacier, an artisan metal and wood workshop based in Saumur, Maine-et-Loire, France. Full company details and registration numbers: see the legal notice.

sections.title: 2. Products
sections.body: Pieces are made by hand, to order, in our workshop. Wood and steel are living materials: slight variations in tone, grain and finish are normal and are not defects.

sections.title: 3. Prices and VAT
sections.body: Prices are shown in euros and are the total amount payable: no tax and no fee is added at payment. The applicable price is the one displayed at the time of the order. Delivery and, where chosen, installation are priced before the order, according to the customer's town (article 6). The workshop's VAT treatment is stated on the invoice.

sections.title: 4. Ordering and payment
sections.body: Catalogue pieces are paid by card at the time of the order, in full: the whole price is charged when ordering, and the invoice is sent automatically. Payment is handled by our provider Stripe; no card data is stored by Auboiacier. For bespoke work quoted individually, the payment terms are set out on that quote. For a gate ordered online, you pay a 40% deposit on the price of the gate when you order. Fitted by the workshop: you also pay the measuring visit, whose price is deducted from the balance; the balance is paid when the fitted gate is handed over, and fitting takes place no later than 10 weeks after the deposit is paid. Delivered by carrier: delivery is added to the price; it depends on the size, weight and bulk of the gate, which travels upright, packed and wedged on a pallet; the balance is paid before dispatch. Collected at the workshop in Saumur: the balance is paid on collection. Without fitting, installation is not included and no motor is offered: motorisation is only sold fitted by the workshop, to guarantee the CE conformity of the whole.

sections.title: 5. Production times
sections.body:
Every piece is made to order: nothing is held in stock. The production time is shown on each piece's own page, on the “Lead time” line — from 3 to 12 weeks depending on the model, the finishes chosen and the season. For bespoke work, the time is stated on the quote.

That time starts on payment and is confirmed to you in writing when you order. Should we exceed it, we tell you: you may then ask us to deliver within a further reasonable period and, if that period is missed, cancel the order and be refunded under article 9.

sections.title: 6. Delivery
sections.body: Delivery in mainland France is made by carrier, at a price calculated from the town, weight and size, shown before ordering and counted once per order; pieces without a delivery option on their page are delivered at no extra charge. It takes place on a date agreed with the customer. On the product page, the customer may ask the workshop to deliver and fit the piece itself: this service is charged according to the distance from Saumur, at the price shown before ordering, and counted once per order. It is the customer's responsibility to check that the piece can be brought to the installation site (access, stairs, doorways). The customer may also choose to collect the order from the workshop in Saumur, by appointment agreed when the piece is ready: collection is free.

sections.title: 7. Right of withdrawal
sections.body:
Under article L221-28 3° of the French Consumer Code, the fourteen-day right of withdrawal does not apply to goods made to the consumer's specifications or clearly personalised. As our pieces are made to order with dimensions, timbers and finishes chosen by the customer, they fall under this exception and cannot be returned or exchanged, unless we expressly agree.

If a piece were sold to you without personalisation and without being built to your measurements, the fourteen-day right of withdrawal would apply as usual: an email would be enough, and the refund would be made under article 9.

A measuring visit booked online is a service: you have fourteen days from the order to withdraw. Because the visit usually takes place before that period ends, we ask you, when ordering, to request this expressly by ticking a box. If you withdraw before the visit, it is refunded in full. Once the visit has been carried out, you can no longer withdraw (article L221-28 1° of the French Consumer Code).

To exercise your right of withdrawal, an email to auboiacier@gmail.com is enough. You may also use the model below (article R221-1):

“To Auboiacier, auboiacier@gmail.com: I hereby give notice that I withdraw from my contract for the sale of the following goods / for the provision of the following service: [order reference]. Ordered on [date] / received on [date]. Name of consumer: [name]. Address of consumer: [address]. Date: [date]. Signature (only if this form is notified on paper).”

sections.title: 8. Warranties
sections.body:
All our pieces are covered by the legal warranty of conformity (two years from delivery) and by the legal warranty against hidden defects (two years from the discovery of the defect). In plain terms: if the piece does not match what was agreed, or if a hidden defect appears, repair, replacement, a price reduction or a refund is at our expense.

The full wording of those rights is reproduced word for word in the official box at the end of these terms. Normal wear, and damage caused by misuse, unsuitable maintenance or modification of the piece, are excluded.

sections.title: 9. Claims, returns and refunds
sections.body:
Any claim should be sent to us by email, with photographs where possible, as soon as the piece arrives. We reply within 48 working hours and agree the next step with you: repair, replacement, price reduction or refund.

Any refund due is paid no later than fourteen days after the right to it arises (withdrawal accepted, order cancelled, sale rescinded). It is made to the payment method used for the order — usually back to your card through Stripe — at no cost to you.

sections.title: 10. Personal data
sections.body:
We only collect what is needed to handle your order: name, email, phone, city and delivery address, order details and amount. Payment is processed by Stripe Payments Europe, emails are delivered by Resend, the site is hosted by Vercel; these providers act on our behalf. Order and invoice data are kept for ten years (accounting obligation). You may access, correct or erase your data, or object to its use, by writing to auboiacier@gmail.com; we answer within a month; you may complain to the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).

Everything else — legal bases, transfers outside the EU, cookies, detailed rights — is set out in our privacy policy.

cgv.garantieTitle: Legal warranty of conformity and hidden defects — official wording
cgv.garantieIntro: The text below is the wording required by French law. It is reproduced as it stands, unchanged.
cgv.garantieBody:
The consumer has two years from delivery of the goods to obtain the benefit of the legal warranty of conformity should a lack of conformity appear. During that period, the consumer need only establish that the lack of conformity exists, not the date on which it appeared.

The legal warranty of conformity entitles the consumer to repair or replacement of the goods within thirty days of the request, free of charge and without major inconvenience.

If the goods are repaired under the legal warranty of conformity, the consumer benefits from a six-month extension of the original warranty.

If the consumer asks for the goods to be repaired but the seller insists on replacement, the legal warranty of conformity is renewed for two years from the date of replacement.

The consumer may obtain a reduction in the purchase price and keep the goods, or end the contract and be refunded in full against return of the goods, if:
1. The trader refuses to repair or replace the goods;
2. The repair or replacement takes place after a period of thirty days;
3. The repair or replacement causes major inconvenience to the consumer, in particular where the consumer definitively bears the cost of taking back or removing the non-conforming goods, or bears the cost of installing the repaired or replacement goods;
4. The lack of conformity persists despite the seller's unsuccessful attempt to bring the goods into conformity.

The consumer is also entitled to a reduction in the price of the goods or to rescission of the contract where the lack of conformity is so serious that an immediate price reduction or rescission is justified. The consumer is then not required to ask for repair or replacement first.

The consumer is not entitled to rescission of the sale where the lack of conformity is minor.

Any period during which the goods are unavailable for repair or replacement suspends the remaining warranty period until the repaired goods are delivered.

The rights set out above arise from articles L. 217-1 to L. 217-32 of the French Consumer Code.

A seller who obstructs in bad faith the operation of the legal warranty of conformity incurs a civil fine of up to 300,000 euros, which may be raised to 10% of average annual turnover (article L. 241-5 of the French Consumer Code).

The consumer also benefits from the legal warranty against hidden defects under articles 1641 to 1649 of the French Civil Code, for two years from the discovery of the defect. That warranty gives a right to a price reduction if the goods are kept, or to a full refund against return of the goods.

confidentialite.title: Privacy policy
confidentialite.intro: This page explains what information the auboiacier.fr website collects about you, why, who receives it, how long we keep it and how to exercise your rights. It applies to quote and contact requests, appointment requests, orders placed online and the customer account.

sections.title: 1. Who is responsible for your data
sections.body:
The data controller is Auboiacier, a metalwork studio in Saumur (49400, Maine-et-Loire, France), represented by Quentin Aumercier. The business's full details (registered name, legal form, SIRET, registered address) appear below where provided, and in the legal notice.

For any question about your data: auboiacier@gmail.com. The studio has no data protection officer: its size and activity do not require one.

sections.title: 2. The data we collect, depending on what you do
sections.body:
You browse the site without filling anything in: we collect no personal data. Your cart is stored in your browser only (section 8). The host's technical logs record your IP address and browser type for a few days at most, to run and protect the site.

You request a quote or contact us: name, email address, phone (optional), town, type of project, your message, and the photos or plans you attach (JPG, PNG or PDF). The language you were browsing in is sent with the request, so we can reply in that language.

You request a measuring appointment: the same information, plus the half-day you would like. If you book and pay for the visit online, your postcode is used to calculate the travel price, and the booking is handled as an order.

You order online: the delivery town (asked in the cart), the order details (pieces, options, dimensions, notes you add), then, on Stripe's payment page: name, email, phone, delivery address and card details. Your card details are entered at Stripe and never pass through our site.

You ask to be told when orders open: your email address and the contents of your cart.

With a request, a sign-up or an order, two more pieces of information may be sent: your answer to the “How did you hear about us?” menu (optional) and, if you reached the site through a campaign link (an Instagram post, a Google ad…), the source, medium and name of that campaign, read from the address of the page you landed on (“utm” parameters). From a Google ad we keep only the fact that you came from one, never its click identifier. This origin is never stored on your device: it stays in the open page and is lost if you reload it.

You open a customer account (optional): your email address, verified by a sign-in link or by Google. If you choose “Continue with Google”, Google sends us your email address and your name, nothing else. In your account you can save your contact details (name, phone, delivery address) so you don't have to type them again, and set aside pieces with their options and dimensions (favourites). This information is kept in the Stripe customer record linked to your email address. There is no password.

We collect nothing else, and no sensitive data. Please do not include any in the free-text field of your messages, and avoid photos in which people can be recognised.

sections.title: 3. Why, and on what legal basis
sections.body:
Answering your quote, contact or appointment request, telling you when orders open and giving you production priority if you asked us to (your email is deleted afterwards), and sending you an acknowledgement: steps taken at your request prior to a possible contract (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR).

Opening and running your customer account (sign-in, saved details, favourites, order tracking): a service you ask us for (Article 6(1)(b)).

Processing your order, taking payment, organising manufacture, delivery or the visit, sending you the confirmation and invoice, handling warranties and after-sales service: performance of the contract (Article 6(1)(b)).

Asking for your opinion, once only: an email about ten days after delivery inviting you, if you wish, to leave a review on the workshop's Google page, with no reminder and nothing offered in return: legitimate interest in following up with our customers (Article 6(1)(f)). Just email us if you would rather not receive it.

Keeping invoices and accounting records: legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c); French Commercial Code).

Protecting the site against abuse (limit on submissions per IP address, anti-bot field, technical logs) and measuring traffic without identifying anyone: legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)), with no impact on your rights and freedoms.

Learning how our customers find us (your answer to the “How did you hear about us?” menu, the campaign you arrived through) and counting, without identifying anyone, the prices calculated, quotes, sign-ups and orders, to decide where to promote the workshop: legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)). The menu is optional; you can also object to the use of the campaign by writing to us.

We do no marketing: no newsletter, no promotional follow-up, no sale or sharing of your data for marketing purposes. If we ever offered a newsletter, it would rely on your consent, freely given and revocable at any time.

sections.title: 4. Who receives your data
sections.body:
Your data is read by the craftsman himself, and processed by the providers below, who act on our behalf, on our instructions and only for the purposes stated:

— Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. (Dublin, Ireland): payment page, payment collection, invoice, refunds, storage of the contact details and delivery address linked to the order, and of your customer account record (saved details, favourites). Stripe also processes some data on its own account (fraud prevention, regulatory obligations), under its own privacy policy: stripe.com/privacy.

— Resend, Inc. (United States): delivery of our emails (acknowledgement, sign-in link, order confirmation, order sheet to the studio, review request after delivery). Resend keeps a copy of sent messages for a few days to track delivery, then deletes it.

— Vercel Inc. (United States): hosting of the site and running of the forms. Vercel sees the IP address and technical logs; if sending an order sheet to the studio fails, the order reference, email and postcode are written to its logs for a few days so that the order is not lost.

— Google (Gmail, Google Ireland Ltd.): our mailbox, where your requests and order sheets arrive.

— Google Ireland Ltd., if you choose “Continue with Google”: Google verifies your identity and sends us your email address and your name. For this sign-in, Google acts under its own privacy policy: policies.google.com/privacy.

— Apple Distribution International Ltd. (Cork, Ireland): the craftsman's calendar (iCloud), where paid measuring appointments appear, with the customer's name, address and phone number.

— Base Adresse Nationale (French public service, api-adresse.data.gouv.fr): only your postcode, sent by our server, to calculate the distance for a measuring visit. No other information goes with it.

We do not sell, rent or pass on your data to anyone. It may be disclosed to an authority where the law requires it.

sections.title: 5. Transfers outside the European Union
sections.body:
Stripe Payments Europe is established in Ireland; it may transfer data to its parent company Stripe, Inc. (United States) which is certified under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, and under standard contractual clauses.

Resend and Vercel are US companies: the data they process may be hosted or accessed in the United States. These transfers are governed by data processing agreements including the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission and, for providers certified under it, by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Where the provider allows it, we choose execution in Europe (site functions in Paris, emails sent from Ireland).

Google Ireland and Apple Distribution International may transfer data to their US parent companies (Google LLC, Apple Inc.) under the same safeguards.

You can obtain a copy of the applicable safeguards by writing to auboiacier@gmail.com.

sections.title: 6. How long we keep it
sections.body:
Quote, contact or appointment request without an order: three years after our last exchange, then deletion. Attached photos and plans follow the same rule.

Orders and paid appointments: order and invoice data are kept for ten years from the end of the financial year, as French accounting law requires (Article L123-22 of the Commercial Code). During the legal warranty period (two years after delivery), they also serve after-sales service.

“Let me know when orders open” requests: until orders open, then deleted at the latest one month later.

Customer account: your saved details and favourites remain for as long as you keep your account. You can change them from the account, and delete it yourself at any time (“Delete my account”, under “Your details”): the record is then erased, except what is linked to an order, which the law requires us to keep. With no order and no activity for three years, we delete it.

Technical logs and anti-abuse counters: from ten minutes to a few days, at the host.

Cart: in your browser only, until you empty it, the order is paid, or you clear the site's data in your browser.

Stripe keeps, on its side, what its own legal obligations require (see its privacy policy).

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.body:
At any time you may ask to see the data we hold about you, to correct it, to have it erased, to restrict its use, to object to processing based on our legitimate interest, and to receive the data you gave us in a machine-readable file (portability). You may also tell us what to do with your data after your death (a right under French law).

An email to auboiacier@gmail.com is enough, preferably from the address used for your request or order. We reply within one month. If there is serious doubt about your identity, we may ask for a means of verification, without requiring a copy of an ID document if another means suffices.

Erasure cannot cover invoices and data the law requires us to keep (section 6): we will tell you so and keep them apart from any other use.

If you are not satisfied with our reply, you may lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the CNIL: www.cnil.fr/en/plaintes, or by post to CNIL, 3 place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, France. If you live in another EU country, you may also contact your local authority.

sections.title: 8. Cookies and browser storage
sections.body:
Unless you open a customer account, this site sets no cookies. It embeds no advertising tracker, no social network button, no third-party video or map.

If you open a customer account, the site sets one cookie, “auboiacier_compte”, which keeps you signed in. It holds your verified e-mail address, an expiry date and, if you signed in with Google, the name Google provided, all signed by the site; nothing else, and no advertising identifier. It is strictly necessary for the service you request — without it you would be signed out on every page — and is therefore exempt from consent (Article 82 of the French Data Protection Act). It lasts thirty days and is deleted as soon as you sign out, or when you clear the site's data in your browser. During the sign-in itself, a second cookie (“auboiacier_passage”) lives for ten minutes: it serves only to check that you are the one who started the sign-in, and disappears straight after.

It also uses a local storage entry in your browser (“auboiacier-panier-v1”) to remember the contents of your cart from one page to the next. And if you leave a product page to sign in, the piece you are configuring (options, dimensions, postcode) is set aside in session storage (“auboiacier-config-v1”), cleared when the tab is closed, so you find it again on your return. These are likewise strictly necessary for the service you request and are exempt from consent. They stay on your device, are not sent to us as such, and you can clear it by emptying the cart or clearing the site's data in your browser.

Audience measurement: this site uses Vercel Web Analytics to count visits and page views. The tool sets no cookies and reads nothing on your device. It does not identify visitors: your IP address and browser name are used only to build an anonymous fingerprint, renewed every day, and are not stored. The data collected (page viewed, country, device type, browser, referring site) is processed on our behalf by Vercel Inc., which hosts the site, on the basis of our legitimate interest in knowing how the site is used (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR), and is not combined with any other data. No consent is required for this measurement; you can block it with a content blocker without affecting the site.

Counters: the site's server also counts the prices calculated, PDF quotes, requests, sign-ups and orders. Each counter carries only the name of the action and, at most, the product family or the general origin of the visit (for example “Instagram” or “no answer”): no name, no e-mail, no IP address, no cookie. It is sent to Vercel Web Analytics with, as the only information about your device, your browser family (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge or other), without its version or your operating system. Paid orders are counted only in the server's technical logs.

The payment page is Stripe's (checkout.stripe.com): Stripe sets its own cookies there, needed for payment and fraud prevention, governed by its cookie policy (stripe.com/legal/cookies-policy).

sections.title: 9. Security
sections.body:
The site is served over HTTPS only. Card details are entered and stored at Stripe, a PCI DSS certified provider; we have no access to them. Access to our mailbox, to Stripe and to the host is protected by password and two-step verification. Form attachments are checked (photo or PDF only) before being forwarded, and the number of submissions per address is limited.

In the event of a data breach likely to affect you, we would inform you and the CNIL within the time limits set by the GDPR.

sections.title: 10. Updates
sections.body: This policy may change if the site or our providers change. The date at the top of the page shows the version in force; a significant change will be announced on the site.

items.q: How long will my piece take?
items.a: Everything is made to order: nothing is held in stock. The lead time is shown on each piece's own page, on the “Lead time” line, and runs from 3 to 12 weeks depending on the model — a chair leaves sooner than a staircase. The exact lead time is confirmed to you in writing when you order.

items.q: Can the lead time be shorter?
items.a: Some steps cannot be rushed: drying the timber, welding, painting, finishing. We can sometimes bring an order forward depending on the workshop schedule — write to us and we will tell you where we stand.

The prices shown in the collection are firm: what you see is what you pay, delivery priced separately by your town. They come from workshop hours and materials, with no middleman. For made-to-measure work (staircase, steel partition, sculpture), the price depends on dimensions and finishes: it is set out in a quote, free of charge.

Yes. The dimensions shown are our usual formats; the workshop makes each piece individually, in length, width, height and shape of top. On tables, window railings and backlit stretch ceilings, a calculator gives the price for your measurements. For anything else, send us your measurements and we will quote.

We deliver anywhere in mainland France by carrier: the price depends on your town, the weight and the size, and appears on the product page as soon as you enter your postcode. Your piece travels protected, and we agree a precise time slot with you. The piece arrives with its notes; a table arrives dismantled, ready to screw together (top, base, hardware). If you would rather the workshop delivered and fitted it itself, choose that on the product page: the price depends on the distance from Saumur, and it all happens in a single trip.

The workshop is in Saumur, in the Maine-et-Loire. We travel up to 200 km from the workshop — Maine-et-Loire, Indre-et-Loire, Deux-Sèvres, Vienne — to measure up and fit, and we deliver furniture anywhere in mainland France. The detail is on the Where we work page.

items.q: How do I care for a wood & steel piece?
items.a: A soft dry cloth day to day. For oiled wood, one coat of hardwax oil a year is enough; a scratch sands out lightly. Painted steel wipes clean with a damp sponge, without abrasives.

Pieces from the collection are paid in full by card when you order, and your invoice is sent automatically. For made-to-measure work on quotation (staircase, steel partition, sculpture), the payment terms are set out on the quote.

items.q: Can I cancel or return an order?
items.a: Our pieces are made to your dimensions and your finishes: French law excludes the fourteen-day right of withdrawal for goods of that kind, so we cannot take them back once production has started. The statutory warranty of conformity and the warranty against hidden defects do apply in full, however: if the piece does not match what was agreed, or has a hidden defect, we repair it, replace it or refund it. The detail is in our terms of sale.

items.q: What if my measurements are wrong?

In the cart, you can add the Measurement guarantee to each piece you measure yourself (railing, backlit ceiling, table), except with fitting by the workshop: {garantiePct} of its price, from {garantieMin} to {garantieMax} per piece. If your measurements were wrong, write to us within 15 days of delivery: the workshop alters or remakes the piece once, to the right size. For no risk at all, the workshop comes and measures at your home, from {prixVisite}. Full details are in article 13 of the terms of sale.

items.q: How is a backlit stretch ceiling fitted?
items.a: The light ceiling hangs on cables attached to four rings screwed into its frame. Your ceiling needs four fixing points strong enough to carry its weight. Up to 230 × 210 cm (Ø 210 cm for the Halo), it ships by carrier; beyond that, it is delivered and fitted at your place by the workshop.

items.q: How is a made-to-measure window railing worked out?
items.a: You enter the window width and the height of the window sill, upstairs or on the ground floor. The workshop works out the number of crosses, the steel section and the gaps between bars to the NF P01-012 standard (a 110 mm ball must not pass below 800 mm from the floor, 180 mm above, with a 3 mm margin), then shows the price.

items.q: What do “handmade” and “made to measure” mean at Auboiacier?
items.a: Every piece is cut, TIG-welded and finished by hand in the Saumur workshop, to the dimensions of your home. There is no stock and no series, and you deal with one person, from measuring to fitting.

lumiere.choixTitle: A light panel or a wall-to-wall stretch ceiling?
lumiere.choixCadre: Our light ceilings are aluminium boxes, complete with their fabric and LEDs, fixed below your existing ceiling. You choose the shape and the size, to the centimetre.
lumiere.choixTendu: A wall-to-wall stretch ceiling is something else: a fabric membrane stretched all round the room, on profiles fixed to the walls, and fitted by a specialist installer.
lumiere.choixPrix: The price shown here is for the whole piece, at its size. The per-square-metre prices you find in guides are for wall-to-wall installation: they do not compare directly.
lumiere.poseBody: The Lucarne and the Halo hang from the ceiling on stainless or steel cables, supplied, attached to four rings screwed into their frame. The LEDs are 24 V strips; the power supplies, connected to the 230 V mains, and the control box are included.
lumiere.lumiereBody: The fabric spreads the light of the LED strips over its whole surface: no hot spot, no hard shadow.
lumiere.piecesBody: Above a dining table or in a large living room.

tables.title: Tables
tables.h1: Bespoke tables in solid wood and steel, handmade in Saumur
tables.intro: The top is solid wood. The base is steel, cut and TIG-welded in the workshop, then painted. You give the length and width to the centimetre, and every product page works out the price at once.
tables.modelesNote: The “from” price is for the smallest size, in the least expensive wood and colour. On the product page, the price follows your configuration.
tables.pietementTitle: The base: steel welded in the workshop
tables.pietementBody: Three designs. Mikado: 80 × 80 mm steel tubes crossed under the top. Croix: a steel X at each end, leaving all the room for legs. Brindille: a bunch of straight steel rods, welded one by one. The Mikado base also carries the river table and the garden table. Every base is welded in the workshop, then painted in the colour you choose.
tables.dimensionsBody: Length and width are up to you, to the centimetre, from {min} cm. The largest one-piece top is {longueur} × {largeur} cm. As a guide, allow about 60 cm of table per guest.
tables.fabricationBody: Nothing is kept in stock. When you order, the steel is cut, welded and ground in the workshop, then painted. The tops of the Mikado, Croix and Brindille tables are finished with hardwax oil; the Mikado Outdoor table gets an outdoor oil, and the river table pairs oak with a pour of epoxy resin. Allow {delai} for making on most models; the exact lead time is on each product page or confirmed with the quote. We deliver anywhere in mainland France by carrier. The workshop can also deliver and fit the table at your home, priced by the distance from Saumur on the product page; or you can collect it from the workshop.
tables.faqTailleA: Allow about 60 cm of table per guest. Catalogue sizes: {formats}. Between two sizes, enter your dimensions: the product page works out the price.
tables.faqBoisA: Oak is the workshop's reference: hard, blond, with a strong grain. Walnut is brown and darker, with a rich grain. Beech is pale, with a fine, tight grain. Pine is the softest: it marks more easily, but a mark sands back out. On the Mikado, Croix and Brindille tables, all four are finished with hardwax oil.
tables.faqEntretienQ: How do I care for an oiled top?
tables.faqEntretienA: Wipe up spills straight away with a soft, barely damp cloth, and put hot dishes on a trivet. When the wood looks dry, a coat of hardwax oil restores its protection; a scratch sands out lightly, on that spot alone.
tables.faqDehorsQ: Can a wooden table stay outdoors?
tables.faqDehorsA: Yes, that is what the Mikado Outdoor table is for: a top of solid oak slats, spaced so rain runs off, finished with an outdoor oil, on a cold-galvanised, lacquered base. Allow one coat of oil a year, or let the wood go grey if you like the patina.
tables.faqHorsQ: Can I have a timber or a shape outside the catalogue?
tables.faqHorsA: Yes, on quotation. Tell us the shape or the timber you want: we adapt the model and price it.
tables.ctaBody: A particular shape, timber or size: describe your project and we will reply with a price.

Between two sizes, enter your own on the product page and the price follows to the centimetre. Delivery is extra, {livraisonMax} at most in mainland France.
tables.hautBody: It shows in what photos don't: the thickness of the top, the section of the steel, the welds. Ours has a solid wood top {epaisseurs} mm thick. The base is welded in the workshop: 80 × 80 mm steel tubes with a 3 mm wall on the Mikado and the Croix; straight steel rods welded one by one on the Brindille. The hardwax oil finish can be touched up where it is marked, without stripping the whole top.

bois.title: Solid wood
bois.h1: Solid wood in our workshop: stair treads, handrails and table tops
bois.intro: In our workshop, solid wood always goes with steel: a tread on a stringer, a handrail on a railing, a top on a welded base. Four timbers are on offer: pine, beech, oak and walnut.
bois.marchesBody: On the central stringer staircase, each tread is a single piece of solid wood 50 mm thick, in pine, beech, oak or walnut. A tread wears where feet land: oak and beech, both hard, mark less quickly than walnut, which is medium-hard, or pine, which is softer.
bois.mainCouranteBody: On the window railing, the handrail can be solid wood, in the same four timbers, finished with hardwax oil. It comes in two forms: a 40 × 40 mm square, grooved underneath to fit over the top rail; or a 60 × 45 mm piece laid on a 60 × 10 mm steel flat bar welded to the top rail, which stiffens it. This is the part your hand touches: wood feels softer there, and less cold than steel. It is also available in steel.
bois.plateauxBody: The Mikado, Croix and Brindille tables have a top in solid pine, beech, oak or walnut; first-grade oak, with no knots and no sapwood, is the workshop's reference. The longer the table, the thicker the top must be so it does not sag: the product page checks that the thickness you choose — 28, 36 or 45 mm — suits the length. The Mikado Outdoor table has a top of spaced oak slats, and the river table a pour of epoxy resin through the oak.
bois.huileBody: Treads, wooden handrails and the tops of the Mikado, Croix and Brindille tables are finished with hardwax oil rather than varnish. The oil soaks into the wood and the wax protects the surface, without forming a film that can flake. The wood keeps its touch and gains a patina over the years. Above all, a mark can be put right without stripping the whole surface: you sand and oil the damaged spot, nothing more. Scratched varnish, by contrast, is hard to touch up in patches. The Mikado Outdoor table gets an outdoor oil instead.
bois.bougeBody: Solid wood follows the humidity of the air: it swells slightly when the air is damp and shrinks back when it is dry. Avoid placing a table against a radiator, or in full sun behind a large window.
bois.atelierTitle: A wood and metal workshop in Saumur
bois.atelierBody: The Saumur workshop draws every piece, welds the steel and works the solid wood with cabinetmaking know-how, from choosing the boards to the finish, before bringing the two together. You keep one point of contact, from the measuring visit to the fitting.
bois.choisirBody: From the least to the most expensive: {ordre}. Oak, hard and golden, is the workshop's reference. Walnut, brown, is the darkest. Beech, pale, has a fine, tight grain. Pine, softer, marks more quickly. The exact price of each wood shows on the product page, at your size.

normesGc.title: Railing height and rules
normesGc.h1: Window railings in France: height, rules and price
normesGc.intro: A low upstairs window, a sill at knee height in an old house: before ordering a railing, you need to know whether it is required, how high its handrail must sit and what gaps it may leave. Here is the rule as the workshop applies it, followed by worked examples priced by the same calculation as the railing's product page.
normesGc.obligatoireTitle: When is a window railing required?
normesGc.obligatoireBody: Upstairs, a window whose sill is less than {seuil} from the floor must be guarded: the French building code requires it in new homes and in building works subject to its rules. In an old house where no such works are planned, adding a railing is therefore not compulsory; the rule is still the safety reference, and the workshop applies it to all its railings. From {seuil} up, it no longer asks for any protection. On the ground floor it asks for none; the workshop keeps the same height there as upstairs.
normesGc.hauteurTitle: How high? It is the handrail that counts
normesGc.hauteurBody: The rule does not set the height of the railing itself, but that of the top of its handrail: at least {loi} above the finished floor of the room, with no tolerance (French building code, article R134-59). The workshop aims for {cible}, to keep a margin. So the top of the handrail is always in the same place, and it is the railing that grows or shrinks with the bottom of the window: its height is {cible}, minus the sill height, minus the gap left under the frame.
normesGc.jourBody: The gap under the frame is the space left between the sill and the bottom of the frame, because a sill is never perfectly flat. The workshop leaves {jour}; when the sill is high and space is short, it reduces it, never below {jourMini}. This gap always stays smaller than {sphere}, the standard's ball.
normesGc.allegeBody: The sill height is measured standing in the room: from the finished floor, with the boards or tiles laid, to the top of the sill where the railing will sit (in the thickness of the wall, window open, at its lowest point). If this sill is lower than the inside ledge, it is the one that counts.
normesGc.croquisLegende: The configurator's sketch, for a window {largeur} wide whose sill is {allege} from the floor: a railing {hauteur} high, set {jourEx} above the sill, the top of its handrail {mainCourante} from the floor.
normesGc.croquisCote: Top of the handrail, from the floor
normesGc.videsBody: The workshop checks the gaps with balls, following the NF P01-012 standard: in a gap that starts less than {zSphere} from the floor, a {sphere} ball must not pass through; in a gap that starts higher, a {sphereHaut} ball. It keeps a {marge} margin: a railing is only sold if every gap is smaller than the ball, less those {marge}. The check is redone for every window, as the number of crosses depends on its width.
normesGc.escaladeBody: Below {escalade} from the floor, the workshop leaves nothing to put a foot on: when the frame starts lower, vertical bars close its lower part, and the crosses only start above.
normesGc.rosaceBody: The rosette counts too. Set where the bars cross, it fills the centre of the cross: a smaller rosette, or none at all, leaves a bigger gap, and fewer designs meet the rule. For each window, the product page only offers the designs that do. A frame with bars only has no crosses, so no rosette: there is none to choose or pay for.
normesGc.videsNote: This is what the site means by “French safety standards”: the height and the gaps, checked window by window. No railing that fails them is sold.
normesGc.exemplesTitle: Worked examples for a window {largeur} wide
normesGc.exemplesIntro: An upstairs window, {largeur} wide, with the product page's starting options: handrail “{bois}”, steel “{teinte}”, rosette “{rosace}”. For each sill height, here is what the workshop calculates, with the design the product page offers first; other compliant designs can be chosen there.
normesGc.ouvrirAria: Open with these measurements: sill at {allege}
normesGc.exemplesNote: Price of one railing, worked out by the same engine as the product page, fixings and fitting guide included. Delivery, fitting or collection from the workshop are chosen next, on the product page.
normesGc.porteFenetreBody: In front of a French window, the bottom of the opening is at floor level, or nearly. The railing then rises from the bottom of the opening to the handrail, and vertical bars close its lower part: that is the first row of the table. It fits between the walls like a window railing, and is ordered the same way, on the same product page.
normesGc.hauteTitle: High windows: a handrail on its own, or nothing
normesGc.hauteBody: When the sill is high, little room is left under the handrail. From {mainSeule} above the floor, even the workshop's smallest frame, with bars, no longer fits: the workshop then makes a handrail on its own, at the same height, on quotation. From {rien}, the sill is almost at handrail height: there is nothing to fit. Where the rule applies, upstairs, protection remains required as long as the sill is below {seuil}.
normesGc.mesurerTitle: Measure yourself, or have the workshop come
normesGc.mesurerBody: Measurements are taken with a tape, in millimetres. The width between the walls, twice: at the sill, then one metre up from the floor. If they differ, the railing follows your walls: the workshop cuts each rail to the width at its level. Then the sill height, from the finished floor. The window height is optional: it checks that the railing fits in the opening. If it does not, the workshop makes it face-fixed, in front of the window, on quotation.
normesGc.visiteBody: If you prefer, the workshop comes to measure: {prixVisite} within {rayonVisite} km of Saumur, then mileage and driving time, up to {rayonMax}. This amount is deducted from your order if you order afterwards.
normesGc.prixBody: The price is worked out from your measurements, on the product page, before any commitment. It depends on the window width, the railing height and the design that meets the rule, then on your choices: the handrail, the rosette and, if you prefer it to the crosses, a glass panel. On the product page: from {depart} for a window {largeurAppel} wide.
normesGc.mainsTitre: Price of the whole railing, by handrail (window {largeur} wide, sill at {allege})
normesGc.rosacesTitre: Price of the whole railing, by rosette (window {largeur} wide, sill at {allege})
normesGc.rosacesNote: With another rosette, the product page sometimes offers another design, and the price changes with it: so the difference is not the same from one window to the next. The product page works it out from your measurements.
normesGc.lotBody: Several windows go in the same basket, each to its own measurements and at its own price.
normesGc.ctaBody: Enter your measurements on the product page: the height, the design and the price show straight away, with a plan preview and a free PDF quote. If you prefer, the workshop comes to measure at your home.
